questions.question: In which of the following locations can you build large dams to generate hydel power?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hilly terrains.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hilly terrains **are suitable for **building large dams** to **generate hydel power** as they have fast-flowing rivers and steep slopes, which create a significant amount of **potential energy.**
 
• The construction of** large dams** requires a significant amount of **water flow, **which is not available in **desert areas.**
 
• Therefore, building large dams in desert areas is **not feasible** for generating hydel power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydel power** is generated by using the** potential energy of falling water** to rotate turbines, which, in turn, generate electricity.
 
• **Large dams** are typically built in** hilly terrains**, where there is a **high volume of water flow**, and the topography creates a significant amount of potential energy.
 
• **Desert areas **are **not suitable **for building large dams as they have low rainfall and a lack of water flow.
 
• **Plains **are** not suitable** for building large dams as the water flow is slow and** does not generate enough potential energy** to generate hydel power.
 
• **Oceans** have a high volume of water flow, but the **water currents are not strong enough** to generate a significant amount of potential energy for generating hydel power.

questions.question: ________ is used to control the demand and supply of money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit control.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit control** is used to control the** demand and supply of money.** 
 
• Credit control refers to the actions taken by the **central bank or monetary authority** to regulate the **availability and cost of credit** in the economy.
 
• By controlling the availability of credit, the central bank can influence the demand for money and therefore** control the money supply.**
 
• Credit control is important for maintaining **price stability and preventing inflation.**
 
• If the central bank allows too much credit to be available, it can lead to an **increase in demand for goods and services**, which can cause prices to rise.
 
• By controlling credit, the central bank can** prevent this** from happening.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the main tools used in credit control is the **setting of interest rates.**
 
• By increasing or decreasing interest rates, the central bank can make** credit more or less expensive**, which can influence the demand for money and the money supply.
 
• Other tools used in credit control include **reserve requirements, open market operations, and moral suasion.**
 
• **Reserve requirements** refer to the amount of money that banks are required to** hold in reserve, **which can influence the amount of credit they can lend.
 
• **Open market operations** involve the** buying and selling of government securities**, which can influence the amount of money in circulation.
 
• **Moral suasion **refers to the **use of persuasion and influence** to encourage banks to adopt certain policies or practices.
 
• **Equity control **refers to the **regulation of ownership** in companies and other assets. 
 
• It is not directly related to the **supply and demand of money.**

questions.question: In which layer of the earth do natural earthquakes occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lithosphere.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural earthquakes** occur in the** lithosphere**, which is the **outermost layer** of the earth.
 
• It includes the crust and the **uppermost part** of the mantle.
 
• The lithosphere is divided into **tectonic plates **that move around on the** asthenosphere**, which is a more fluid layer beneath it.
 
• The movement of these plates creates **stress on the rocks,** which can cause them to break and **release energy **in the form of earthquakes.
 
• The lithosphere is also where most of the **volcanic activity** on earth occurs, as magma rises up from the** mantle** and reaches the surface through cracks in the crust.
 
• The inner core is a solid, dense ball of** iron and nickel **at the center of the earth.
 
• It is **too deep and too hot** for earthquakes to occur there.
 
• The mesosphere is the **layer beneath the lithosphere,** and it is too solid for earthquakes to occur there as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **asthenosphere** is a** plastic layer beneath the lithosphere,** where the rocks are partially molten and can flow.

 
 
• It plays a key role in** plate tectonics** and the movement of the** earth's crust.**
 
 
 
• The** inner core** is the **hottest part of the earth**, with temperatures estimated to be as high as **5,500 degrees Celsius**.
 
 
• It is also under **immense pressure,** which keeps it solid despite the high temperatures.
 
 
 
• The **mesosphere** is a relatively **unknown layer of the earth**, as it is difficult to study due to its **depth and lack of seismic activity.**
 
 
• It is thought to be a** transition zone** between the rigid lithosphere and the more fluid asthenosphere.

questions.question: The proportion of India's GDP contributed by the ___________ sector increased in the period from 11.8 per cent in 1950-51 to 24.6 per cent in 1990-91.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**industrial.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** industrial sector **contributed significantly to** India's GDP**, increasing from** 11.8% in 1950-51 to 24.6% in 1990-91.**
 
• This growth was due to the **government's focus** on industrial development during the** post-independence period.**
 
• The industrial sector includes **manufacturing, mining, and construction industries.**
 
• The growth in the industrial sector led to a** decrease in the share of the agricultural sector** in India's GDP.
 
• The services sector also saw significant growth during this period, but it was not as significant as the** industrial sector.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **defence sector** is** not directly related** to GDP contribution.
 
• The **services sector** did see **significant growth **during this period, but it was not as significant as the industrial sector.
 
• However, it is still an** important contributor **to India's GDP.
 
• The** agricultural sector** saw a **decrease in its share of India's GDP **during this period due to the growth in the industrial and services sectors.
 
• However, it still remains an **important sector** for India's economy.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution talks about the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 149.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 149 **of the Indian Constitution talks about the **duties and powers** of the **Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)**.
 
• The CAG is responsible for **auditing the accounts **of the **Union and State governments, local bodies, and other public authorities**.
 
• The CAG is also empowered to conduct** performance audits **of government programs and schemes to ensure their effectiveness and efficiency.
 
• The CAG reports its findings to the **President or Governor,** who then places them before the** Parliament or State Legislature, **respectively.
 
• The CAG is an independent constitutional authority appointed by the **President of India **and holds office for a term of six years or until the **age of 65**, whichever is earlier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** As per the Article 160** of the Indian Constitution Discharge of the functions of the Governor in certain contingencies The President may make such provision as he thinks fit for the discharge of the functions of the Governor of a State in any contingency not provided for in this Chapter.
 
• **Article 148** deals with the appointment of the **Comptroller and Auditor General of India.**

• **Census** is a process of collecting, analyzing, and publishing** demographic, social, and economic data** of a country's population.
 
• The** last Census of 2011 **was the **15th Census of India** and was conducted under the** Census Act of 1948.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Since **1949,** it has been managed by the** Ministry of Home Affairs**, Government of India, through the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.**
 
• The** 1948 Census of India Act**, which predates the Indian Constitution, has been used to conduct all censuses since **1951.**
 
• The Union Government is not required by the **1948 Census of India Act** to carry out the Census on a specific date or to make the results available within a specified timeframe.

questions.question: When did Ashoka, the Mauryan ruler, die?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**232 BC.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka** was one of the most powerful emperors of the **Mauryan dynasty,** ruling from** 268 to 232 BC.**
 
• He is known for his conversion to** Buddhism** and his efforts to spread the religion throughout his empire.
 
• Ashoka's reign was marked by significant **political and social reforms,** including the establishment of a network of hospitals and the promotion of religious tolerance.
 
• He died in **232 BC**, and was succeeded by his** son, Kunala.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **third Mauryan Emperor of Magadha** was Ashoka, who ruled over the Indian subcontinent.
 
• His empire, which had **Pataliputra as its capital, **stretched across a sizable portion of the Indian subcontinent, from what is now **Afghanistan **in the west to what is now **Bangladesh** in the east.
 
• According to Ashoka's edicts, **Kalinga** was subjugated by him following a bloody battle in his **eighth regnal year** (approximately 260 BCE).
 
• Following this, Ashoka committed himself to spreading the **edicts' main idea of "dhamma," or morality.**
 
• The edicts of Ashoka suggest that he began to lean more and more toward **Buddhism **a few years after the Kalinga War.

questions.question: In ______, the East India Company acquired a charter from the ruler of England, Queen Elizabeth I, granting it the sole right to trade with the East.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1600.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **East India Company **was granted a charter by** Queen Elizabeth I in 1600**, giving it a monopoly on **English trade** with the East Indies.
 
• The charter gave the company the power to **establish factories** (trading posts) in India and to **export goods** such as **spices, silk, and tea** back to England.
 
• The company grew in** power and influence** over time, eventually becoming the **de facto ruler** of much of India by the mid-18th century.
 
• The East India Company played a major role in British imperialism, shaping the** economic, political, and cultural landscape **of India and other parts of the world for centuries to come.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Incorporated in** England** in** 1600** and later becoming British, the East India Company (EIC) was dissolved in **1874.**
 
• It was established to facilitate trade with** East Asia and the East Indies** in the Indian Ocean region.
 
• The company colonized parts of **Southeast Asia and Hong Kong** in addition to seizing control of a sizable portion of the **Indian subcontinent.**
